clue.text: Teacher's first to get into sadly messy theory

indicators.note: to get into tells us the teacher's initial is placed inside the jumbled letters
sadly suggests the word messy is in a bad state, so its letters are rearranged
first, attached to Teacher's, asks for only that word's opening letter

explanation.surface: A teacher's first effort at a theory turns out sadly muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MESSY to SYSEM, and 'to get into' puts T, the first of 'Teacher's', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised set of principles or ideas, which is what a theory is.

clue.text: Abandon stunted trees

definitions.meaning: to give up on a plan, as in calling off a mission
low-growing bushes and undersized trees covering rough ground

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for cancelling it, and scrub is also land covered in low, stunted vegetation.

clue.text: Restaurants having scruffy attire? Rot!

indicators.note: scruffy describes something untidy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea that Italian eateries come with shabby clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' rearranges the nine letters of ATTIRE and ROT together. The plural is the Italian form, matching 'Restaurants'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eating place; the Italian plural ends in -ie.

clue.text: Tower near ground in us college

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the college's initials

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, an American college

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down or crushed, tells us the word near is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tower stands on land close to an American university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns NEAR into NARE, and 'in' sets that inside MIT. 'us' stands for US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Man with place in queue — useful source of advice?

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for place inside the word for a queue

parts.note: a line is a queue of people waiting
Pl. is the standard abbreviation for Place in street addresses

explanation.surface: A man holding a spot in a queue proves a handy source of guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone service people ring for guidance or support with a problem is a helpline.

clue.text: Employ on board son in Cornish town and be touched

annotationWithheld.why: Employ on board son in Cornish town and be touched (4,1,5,5): HAVE A CREW (employ on board) + LOOE (Cornish town) gives one S short; 'son' would have to supply the S in both SCREW and LOOSE, doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Employ on board son in Cornish town and be touched

clue.text: Liberation of gulag, say, brought up cases?

indicators.note: liberation of the word gulag frees its letters to be rearranged
brought up, in a down clue, means the abbreviation is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: The freeing of a Soviet labour camp is raised as an example in legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberation of' rearranges GULAG to LUGGA, and 'brought up' turns EG into GE. The question mark flags the definition as a pun: suitcases rather than court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage, the suitcases and bags a traveller carries, is luggage.

clue.text: Novel showing Russian tops in having overturned edict

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name, used for a Russian in crosswords

indicators.note: tops in a down clue are the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A book shows a Russian leader cancelling a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's Ivanhoe is a historical novel set in medieval England.

clue.text: Teatime's spent around new cafe

indicators.note: around tells us the jumbled letters wrap round the letter for new
spent suggests the word is worn out and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teatime has passed by the time someone reaches a newly opened cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' rearranges TEATIMES (from 'Teatime's') to ESTAMIET, and 'around' puts that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar, a word familiar from the First World War.

clue.text: Continue on road in Minnesota

parts.note: re means on, concerning or about

indicators.note: in places the road's letters within the state abbreviation

parts.note: MN is the postal abbreviation for Minnesota
the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A traveller keeps driving along a highway in Minnesota.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write it AI.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay or carry on, so it can mean to continue.

clue.text: Attentive woman with enormous figure about 50

parts.note: Vi is a short woman's name, from Violet

indicators.note: about tells us the big figure goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: a giant is a huge figure
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A large woman of about fifty keeps a watchful eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an approximate age, but it places GIANT around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and watchful for danger is being vigilant, the same as paying close attention.

clue.text: A tribe unsettled about account revealing sources of illness

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for account
unsettled means disturbed, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agitated tribe hears a report of where diseases come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges A TRIBE to BTERIA, and 'about' puts that round AC: B-AC-TERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs, microscopic organisms that can cause disease, are bacteria.

clue.text: Some bemoan the most religious song

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain churchgoers complain loudly about one particular hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'bemoan' through 'the' into 'most'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral composition set to sacred words, sung in church services.

clue.text: Love picture about English renegade — typical of stagy work?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: about tells us the word for a picture surrounds the other two pieces

parts.note: pic is short for picture
a rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side

explanation.surface: A romantic film about an English traitor sounds like melodrama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is zero in tennis, written O. 'about' wraps the picture word round the other two. The question mark admits that 'stagy work' is a loose description of opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged musical drama, so something characteristic of it, often overblown, is described as operatic.

clue.text: Retired copper and manager in old company getting Italian dish

indicators.note: in places the turned-round pieces inside the letters for old and company
Retired in a down clue means drawn back, so these pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: A former policeman and his boss join an old firm and get something Italian to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the copper and manager pieces around to give SSOBUC, and 'in' puts that inside the letters for old company.
explanation.definitionFit: Osso bucco is a Milanese stew of braised veal shanks, its name meaning bone with a hole.

clue.text: Woman recalling endless requirement with tale

indicators.note: recalling, as in calling back, tells us the pieces are read in the opposite direction
endless means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a need is a requirement
a lie is a made-up tale

explanation.surface: A woman remembers a story that was always needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts NEED to NEE, and 'recalling' turns NEE plus LIE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Rewarding version of vital cure

indicators.note: version of suggests a different form of the following words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new form of essential medicine pays off handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges the letters of VITAL and CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative venture is profitable, one that rewards those involved with money.

clue.text: Courses taken by trains, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, so a word that is said the same way is entered

parts.note: suites are trains or retinues of attendants

explanation.surface: Lessons are attended by people travelling by rail, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: A suite, like a train, is a group of followers attending a dignitary. Sweets are the dessert courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Puddings served at the end of a meal are called sweets in Britain, and are courses of the meal.

clue.text: Theologian formulated measures English rejected

indicators.note: formulated means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion drafted measures that the English turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' tells us E (English) is removed from MEASURES, and 'formulated' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderius Erasmus was a Dutch Renaissance scholar and theologian.

clue.text: Odd testing area below street

indicators.note: below in a down clue means the second piece comes under the first in the grid

parts.note: a range is an area for testing weapons or missiles

explanation.surface: It seems peculiar to put a weapons-testing ground under a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means unusual or peculiar, the same as odd.

clue.text: Official devising race tour

indicators.note: devising means creating something new, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat is planning a cycle race around the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devising' rearranges the eight letters of RACE and TOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is an administrator in the European Union's institutions, a kind of official.

clue.text: Guy with ring, decorative item

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock them, and to rib is to tease
a band is a ring, as in a wedding band

explanation.surface: A man with a ring is showing off his ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but here it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribband is an old spelling of ribbon, a decorative strip of fabric.

clue.text: Stand around borders of village and work hard

indicators.note: around tells us the word for stand goes round the two letters

parts.note: to bear something is to stand or tolerate it

indicators.note: borders of asks for the outside letters, the first and last, of the word village

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates life on the edge of a village and grafts away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' gives V and E, the first and last letters of 'village', and 'around' puts BEAR round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is an idiom for working industriously, like the busy animal.

clue.text: Dog unleashed abroad in both directions

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the two direction letters

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two directions

indicators.note: unleashed means let loose, so the letters of abroad run free and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog runs off its lead while overseas, going this way and that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unleashed' gives ABRADO, and 'in' puts that between L and R, left and right, the two directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labrador is a breed of retriever dog.

clue.text: Playful fellow departing? That's dangerous

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so the letter for the fellow is taken out

parts.note: frisky means playful and lively

explanation.surface: A frisky man leaving is said to be hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful fellow departing' gives FRISKY with the F removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky carries a chance of harm, so it is dangerous.

clue.text: Male graduate in us property, a military type

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the American word for a property

parts.note: a condo is an American word for a flat or apartment, a US property
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A man with a degree living in an American apartment turns out to be a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' stands for US, the United States, whose word condo means a flat. 'in' places M and MA within CONDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, someone in a special military unit.

clue.text: Hatred that's total in a revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: A rebel's hostility is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives NIMUS, which follows the A; 'in' looks like a link word but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostility or ill will, a synonym for hatred.

clue.text: Out-of-date boots Lee repaired

indicators.note: repaired means fixed up into a new state, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Lee had his old boots mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges the letters of BOOTS and LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete describes something no longer in use, outdated.

clue.text: Smart doctor? Yes at work around San's opening

indicators.note: around tells us the jumbled letters go round the initial
at work means busy, so the letters of yes are stirred about and rearranged
opening asks for only the first letter of the word San's

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed doctor says yes to working at a sanatorium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges YES to ESY, and 'around' places it round S, the first letter of 'San's'. A san is a sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and formal.
